segments.text: Hi everyone! I'm Nikki, co-founder at Jexo  and today I'll be talking about one of the
prioritization techniques - ICE. If you are  completely new to prioritization techniques, I
highly recommend to you to watch our introduction  video, the link is in the description below. And now
back to the prioritization techniques. ICE is short for Impact, Confidence, and Effort. This technique
was initially developed for prioritizing growth  experiments but grew in popularity and is now also
used for prioritizing product backlogs, usually  when you don't have enough usage data available.
Let's have a look on the metrics we need to fill for this method. The first of them is Impact. When
assigning the impact values, ask yourself the  question: how much does this contribute to our
goal? And the goal is anything your team or company  are trying to achieve. You might be focusing on
increasing customer retention, increasing the brand  awareness or the quality of your product. The next
metric is Confidence. Because some people are being  very optimistic about the impact, this metric will
bring us closer to the ground. When filling this  one up, ask yourself the question: how confident
are you that this will work and deliver the impact  you assigned earlier? Usually when there are data
that can become the assigned impact, Confidence is  high. If there are no data, then confidence is low.
The last metric to look at is Ease. With this one  we are evaluating how difficult it is to deliver
the task. The common mistake when assigning this  metric is that people don't consider all parties
involved in delivering the task. What may seem to  be easy to develop, might not be always easiest
to design or test, in the opposite. When we assign all  metrics, we can calculate the final priority score.
Multiply Impact, Confidence, and Ease and you have  it. The higher the priority score of the item,
the higher on your list it gets. And that's it!  Simple. Now let's have a look on the real example.
I have an example backlog of tasks to prioritize  in Jira and I'm using Foxly app to record the
metrics. Let's first fill Impact. To fill this one  up, let's say that our team goal is to increase
amount of trials that transform  to the paying customers. For Onboarding video the
Impact is going to be fairly high because we saw  that not many users get to the Aha moment fast
enough. The Confidence is high as well because  we don't have onboarding in the app and adding
this quick fix will help. We also get feedback  from customer interviews and from private demos
where people got confused because of lack  of onboarding. And the Effort is medium. Next
in the row is Navigation redesign. the Impact of  this one is medium. On the interview some people
got confused by the icons and couldn't find  their way around. And the Confidence is low.
Although we have done some interviews, we don't  really know that this will help and the effort
is large. We will need to go through several design  sessions, user testing and development to deliver
this. The last task to prioritize is Adding new  filters. The impact of this one is fairly low. Few
customers ask for new filters but none of them  seem to be a showstopper to continue the trial.
The Confidence is medium as we don't have  enough data to back up our decision, and the
Effort is medium as well because it will require  help of design and development to deliver this.
Now, when we are done with the prioritizing,  we can order our list by the priority score
and see what item is the  most important to start with.
If you are looking for a backlog prioritization  tool that integrates with Jira, where you can
use this template, you can try our app Foxly.  It's really fun and easy to use and helps keep
everyone in your team and stakeholders up to  date with their latest priorities. If you feel
that ICE prioritization technique might not be  the right one for you and your team, have a look
on our other videos where we introduce other  ones, like RICE, Weighted Shortest Job First (WSJF), Value
vs Effort, or Quick Wins method. See you in the  next video and in the meantime happy prioritizing!
